newsitem.title: GERMANY: SAP profit surge helps lift German share market.
newsitem.headline: SAP profit surge helps lift German share market.

text.p: Surprisingly strong earnings figures from software developer SAP AG delighted an already upbeat German stock market Friday morning, helping prices to approach record levels in early bourse trade.
The DAX index was up 18.54 points at 3,035.86 points at 1015 GMT, not far off its alltime high of 3,041.55, amid heavy trade and gains of over 12 percent on SAP.

The software group, once the darling of the stock market but under pressure in recent months amid more downbeat results forecasts, shocked the market by beating its own estimates for 1996 with profits up 40 percent at 567 million marks and sales up 38 percent at 3.72 billion.
Its DAX-listed preferred shares were up 27 marks at 249 marks after hitting a high of 258.80 in pre-bourse trade.

The broader market was boosted from the start by Wall Street's overnight rally and a firm start by Bunds, as well as strong first-half earnings from luxury car-maker Porsche, aslo a big winner in early trade.
"This is something like the optimal set-up for us and when you have SAP adding to that, things are pretty ideal," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"Those were tremendous numbers from SAP," a Munich dealer said. "They gave the market a wonderful boost."

Porsche preferred stock was up 75 marks, or 5.5 percent, at 1,445 marks, after the company announced first-half profit of 36 million marks and said it would increase its capacity to satisfy demand for its new Boxster model.
Dealers said activity would likely quieten down as the session continued, as the wait for key U.S. economic data in the afternoon begins again.
U.S. fourth quarter GDP figures and the Chicago purchasing managers index for January are due at 1330 GMT.
